1.sofaString: 411	Pt, ***, is a 10 year old male who is diagnosed with DORV with complete AVSD and side-by-side great vessels s/p non-fenestrated fontan, now with history of ECMO, Heartmate 3, and trach. He is also dialysis dependent, on HD. He is being referred for heart/ kidney transplant evaluation.      Information for this assessment was obtained through an interview with the pt's father (with assistance from interpreter) and review of the medical records.   *** was watching a video on his Ipad and did not participate in the evaluation.  He was also being administered pills, and vomited while trying to take them.      Living situation:  **, ***, lives with his mother and half sisters in *******, **.  They reside in ** *********. Per record review, dad resides with a friend. However, dad states that he resides in the same household as mom and the children.  He provided a second ******* ** ***** * ********** **, Lot 47, ******* ** *****. However, he states this is just a mailing address.  He states there is no smoking in the home.  However, he states that mom does smoke outside.        Demographics:  Mother: **** *********  DOB:  **/**/****        Age:  48  Employment:  Currently works at a gas station in *****   Phone:  ***-***-**** (cell)     Father: ***** *****  DOB:  **/**/****    Age:  50  Employment:  Currently unemployed. Previously worked as heavy machinery operator.   Phone:  ***-***-**** (cell)     Siblings:  ****-******, ******* *******, Age 17  ****-******, ****** *******, Age 19      Support systems:  Parents have been together for 10 years but are not married.  Dad states that they have no other support persons outside of them and the 2 half siblings.  The father of the step-siblings resides in ****.  Dad states that there is an uncle who resides nearby the family. However, he does not help to provide support. Dad disclosed that they do have some friends who are able to occasionally provide a small amount of financial support. He was provided $50 to assist with his food expenses while here in Gainesville with patient.        Transportation is a challenge for the family.  Dad does not have a car. Mom does have a car. However, it is an older car and is not reliable for length of travel needed to come to Gainesville.  Dad states mom will need to take the bus in order to come to Gainesville to visit.  It is likely they would need to rely on Medicaid transport for follow up appointments.          *** is in the 3rd grade. Dad reports that hospital homebound ********* was inconsistent.  He was not able to provide more explanation.  *** has been admitted to outside hospital since ****** ** ****.  *** presents as a strong willed child who is difficult to engage in tasks that he does not want to do.            Dad denies any religious preference. He states they do not ****** to a church, but that he practices his beliefs on his own. He denies any objection to blood products or transfusions.     Course of illness:     *** was born with prenatally diagnosed congenital heart disease.  He is diagnosed with DORV   with complete AVSD and side-by-side great vessels. He underwent a Bidirectional ***** at 9 months of age.  He underwent non-fenestrated fontan at the age of 4.  He presented to *** ******** ********'s Hospital in ****** **** for worsening ****** physiology, ventricular dysfunction and transplant evaluation. EF was 20% and he was found to have an LV thrombus. During a TEE as a part of the work up, he became bradycardiac, then pulseless and required brief CPR. He recovered nicely from this event with milrinone and dopamine for support. His end organ function was normal and he was listed on UNOS wait-list Status 1A for heart transplant on */**/**. Unfortunately the following day he had a Vfib cardiac arrest that required over an hour of **** and eventual VA ECMO cannulation. His ECMO course/arrest was complicated by continued site bleeding as well as an ischemic right occipital lobe infarct (non-hemorrhagic) and possible venous sinus thrombosis. This was accompanied by left sided weakness/paresis. He was subsequently changed to UNOS Status 7. Decision was made to transition to VAD support. He underwent HeartMate 3 implantation (LV apical implant to ascending aorta) on */**/**.     He was extubated again in early ********, but soon developed a massive GI bleed and required re-intubation.  He required HFOV for 5 days and remained on invasive ventilation for the next several weeks. He became significantly ************* during this period and eventually underwent tracheostomy on **/**/**.  He has since been able to wean off of vent support. Currently his trach is capped continuously.       He has also had issues with AKI since the extended arrest and CPR. He is currently on a MWF HD schedule.       He has been followed by PT, OT, and SLP. He has made great strides in his mobility since his initial CVA. He is able to walk a few steps with a walker. He does require assistance to stand,/transfer, etc. His last swallow eval in ***** showed aspiration with thin liquids, but no aspiration w thickened liquids or solid foods.      He is now being evaluated for heart/ kidney transplant.          Financial Situation:     *** is covered by Medicaid Simply insurance.  Currently the family is supported by the income of mom.  Records indicate she is working fulltime. However, dad states she is working part-time and that the hours are variable and not consistent. Dad states they are unable to meet their financial needs on her income. Dad is unemployed currently. *** does not currently have SSI. Due to the extended admission, he would be receiving only $30/ monthly until discharged.    Dad reports that they do receive food ******. However, he believes they need to update their information and he is unsure if this benefit will be continued.  Dad denies interest in fundraising, as he states they do not have a network of support for this. He states they do have some friends who occasionally can give a small amount of financial support to them.       Family History:     There is no significant medical history in the family. Dad has a history of hypertension.  Mom reportedly has issues with her blood sugar.            There is no reported significant family mental health history.  However, dad states that mom is a 'nervous' person. He states she is stressed. He reports that he is able to handle stress ok.  *** reportedly had a psych eval at *** ********.  However, dad is unable to provide any information about this. He states *** ***** appropriately when dad is at bedside. He states *** has difficulty if dad is not present.     The family denies any significant history of substance abuse.  Dad does state ** drinks socially. In addition, he states that mom does smoke cigarettes.  There is no reported history of DV or involvement with DCF.  Dad does have a felony history from 2021 for grand theft.      Adherence:  There are concerns for adherence. There have been documented concerns from the outside hospital regarding dad not abiding by some of the medical recommendations, particularly in regards to *** being given oral nutrition and abiding by fluid restrictions.  It was observed that *** has difficulty taking some pills by mouth, as evidenced by him gagging and vomiting while attempting to do so.      There are also concerns for adherence due to the lack of support persons and lack of reliable transportation.       Assessment and recommendations:     Dad expressed belief that *** does not need a kidney transplant because he is making urine on his own.  He does believe *** needs a heart however. He states he is able to take care of the HeartMate 3, and was trained adequately on how to do this.       Dad expresses a great deal of stress regarding the financial situation. He is expressed a desire to find a part-time job. However, he is limited in opportunities because of only speaking and reading Spanish.  There is much more opportunity for him in ***** area.  He is also concerned for the loss of the limited income they do have, if mom comes to Gainesville.  Should *** receive transplant here, the family would need to remain in Gainesville for at least 6 weeks after discharge for close monitoring and follow up. This would be a continued hardship for the family.           IMPRESSION:     (Low Risk - 1; Moderate Risk - 2; High Risk - 3; Severe Risk - 4)     Home Environment/Transportation -  3  Family Background & Social Support -  4  Financial/Insurance  - 3  Mental Health/Substance Abuse - 2  Involvement with *** Enforcement/Child Protection -  2  Adherence - 4  Understanding of medical situation & transplant process -  2  Health Literacy -  3  Coping Skills - 2     Total:  25  High Risk     The family scores as high risk in regards to psychosocial contra-indicators to transplant.       Recommendations are listed below:     Recommendations:  *It appears it would be in patient and family's best interest to transfer back to ***** where they can be closer to their support system.  Patient could potentially discharge with HeartMate 3 and receive outpatient HD.  If family is able to consistently care for both of these, they would demonstrate better ability to move forward with transplant.    Provide ongoing education to the family about heart transplant and post-transplant care.  Use teachback method to confirm understanding  *Provide fundraising and financial resources to assist the family with expenses that arise secondary to child's extended admission   *Assist with connecting child and family with counseling and supports that will assist in positive coping skills        ****** ******** LCSW *****  Pediatric Heart/ Lung Transplant Team  ***-***-****
